title: Research
text:
Pennsylvania State University — Mechanical Engineering
Ph.D. | August 2026


My dissertation research used predictive walking simulations to investigate how torque capability limitations can contribute to gait changes associated with post-stroke walking.


Developed additional capabilities for a 2D lower-body skeletal model in MATLAB using hybrid zero-dynamics (HZD)-based control to perform two-step periodic predictive walking simulations, including improvements to foot-ground interactions, impacts, walking mechanics, and optimization frameworks.




How do unilateral torque capability limitations affect walking mechanics and gait asymmetry?
How do torque-rate limitations influence double-support time?
What walking objectives and underlying mechanics may contribute to reduced step lengths, asymmetries, and increased double-support time beyond energetic cost?




MATLAB · Predictive simulation · Optimization · HZD-based control · Biomechanics · Physics modeling

title: Nicholas Yaple
text:
I am a mechanical engineer with a Ph.D. background in predictive simulation, optimization, and robotic control. My work spans physics-based modeling, control systems, MATLAB/Simulink, Python, and robotics—connecting computational methods with engineering systems and experimental results.

title: Projects
text:
2025–Present
Designed a modified control approach for an existing robotic arm using human arm positions captured from a single camera. The system integrates Python, OpenCV, MediaPipe pose detection, ROS 2, and machine-learning components.

Captures and interprets human arm position using camera-based perception.
Connects perception outputs with robotic control through ROS 2.
Explores practical integration of sensing, software, and robot motion.

Technologies: Python · OpenCV · MediaPipe · ROS 2 · Machine learning
